claims.claim: Reviewers describe performance issues including stuttering, lag, and poor optimization.

citations.review_text:
Stay away from the GTA Trilogy Definitive Edition if you actually want to enjoy these games. If you want the real experience, play the original versions on PC or consoles. Rockstar completely ruined what the original games were and replaced them with this buggy, poorly optimized mess.

The mission design is already frustrating enough, but the bugs make everything even worse. For example, during a mission where you're supposed to enter a factory and kill enemies, you automatically get a wanted level. When trying to complete the race challenge, you can end up with a 5-star wanted level, with cops constantly shooting at you. Before you even reach the finish line, your car is likely to explode because of all the damage.

The vehicle handling is terrible, NPC drivers randomly crash straight into you for absolutely no reason, and the overall driving experience is frustrating. It's the same kind of garbage experience you get with GTA IV's terrible PC optimization.

And don't even get me started on Rockstar's so-called Definitive Edition. They somehow managed to make the Trilogy look worse in several aspects, introduce new bugs, mess up the original atmosphere and deliver an experience that feels like a cheap, unfinished remaster rather than a proper upgrade.

Performance is another disaster. You need proper community mods and fixes just to get the game running at 120 FPS without constant frame drops. Even on high-end hardware, you can experience random drops to 90–100 FPS and noticeable stuttering.

Honestly, I regret buying this version. I can't even get a refund, and this is probably one of the biggest mistakes I've made when purchasing a game. Rockstar took three classic masterpieces and turned them into a buggy, unoptimized mess. Save your money and stay away from this version.
Simply because these mobile game developers cannot do a job properly. Stuttering should not be an issue yet somehow it is. This game ran on a PS2 ffs. How can a PC not give a smoother experience?!

the game is good as for the story but the optimisation is bad guys

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features a large open map with plenty of side activities and things to do outside of missions.

citations.review_text: "Ah sh*t, here we go again!" San Andreas is easily one of my favorite GTA games. There's just something special about CJ, Grove Street, and the massive world Rockstar created. From Los Santos to San Fierro and Las Venturas, there's an insane amount of things to explore and get into. The Definitive Edition gives the game a fresh coat of paint with improved visuals, lighting, textures, and updated controls. It's great being able to revisit this classic with some modern improvements while still enjoying the original experience. What makes San Andreas so memorable is the sheer amount of content. You have gang wars, territory takeovers, customizable vehicles, properties, businesses, side activities, and an entire story filled with unforgettable characters and hilarious moments. You can spend hours just messing around without even touching the main missions. CJ's journey is one of the best stories in the GTA series, and the soundtrack is packed with classics that make driving around the map even better. The Definitive Edition isn't perfect, and there are still some issues, but getting to experience San Andreas again is absolutely worth it.
Ovb an amazing game for the time it was produced in, enormous map and a shit ton of stuff to do when you're not on a mission.

Genuine Shite and I'm not just talking about how it is a remake and going to glaze the OG because the story sucks, the missions are almost as bad as GTA3 and the characters (one of the most important parts) are mostly all unlikeable. Would not recommend and probably not even the OG. Vice City and Vice City Stories are 100x better than this.

Edit: I do love how much there is to do in this game. The Map feels big and I really love Las Venturas. I still stand by the majority of the story being mid so far.

While Rockstar has done some work after the disaster that was the initial release by "GroveStreet Games", the end resulting product is still lacking compared to the original. With mods, you could make the original look as good or better than this version. Additionally, this version contains fewer songs due to licenses that were not renewed and some shoddy graphical work due to the undisclosed generative AI used to quickly import and "update" the models.

The last new issue is unlike the original game, this one also requires the terrible Rockstar app integration and sign-in. Stuttering is also present for no apparent reason after a random amount of time and it doesn't go away but instead progressively gets worse.

All in all, it's bully tactics by Rockstar to withhold the superior original version of this title while charging a premium for an inferior product. I would recommend acquiring the original version by whatever other means necessary, such as the used market or console (PS2/Xbox).

While Rockstar has done some work after the disaster that was the initial release by "GroveStreet Games", the end resulting product is still lacking compared to the original. With mods, you could make the original look as good or better than this version. Additionally, this version contains fewer songs due to licenses that were not renewed and some shoddy graphical work due to the undisclosed generative AI used to quickly import and "update" the models.

The last new issue is unlike the original game, this one also requires the terrible Rockstar app integration and sign-in. Stuttering is also present for no apparent reason after a random amount of time and it doesn't go away but instead progressively gets worse.

All in all, it's bully tactics by Rockstar to withhold the superior original version of this title while charging a premium for an inferior product. I would recommend acquiring the original version by whatever other means necessary, such as the used market or console (PS2/Xbox).

Honestly, the current state of the game is fine and fun to play if you keep your expectations realistic.

The original was legendary, but playing at 25 fps with heavy fog and short render distance doesn't really hold up anymore. Roaming San Andreas in 4K at 80+ fps with high-res models and updated controls makes replaying it a lot of fun. It is definitely easier with checkpoints, but as someone who already finished the original multiple times, I liked the refreshed experience. Just like the rest of the trilogy, it stuttered out of the box until I used a manual vulkan dll fix, but after that, I played through the entire story without a single crash or major game-breaking bug.

Cons:
- Requires a manual vulkan dll fix to get rid of stuttering
- Missing radio tracks
- Annoying keybinding and control bugs
- Garages still randomly dismiss stored vehicles

claims.claim: Reviewers state that aircraft controls for planes and helicopters are overly sensitive and harder to handle compared to the original version.

citations.review_text:
GTA San Andreas is a great game. For me, it is the best in all Grand Theft Auto series, up to this very moment. Yet, the Definitive Edition here... is a seriously overpriced rip-off aimed at those nostalgia players who still care about 100% completion, achievements and such nonsense.

Two major things, that frustrate me the most in the Definitive Edition, are the remade controls, especially the flight and other steering controls settings, and the broken math of role-play parameters such as fat, muscle and hunger complex, lung capacity, and other bars. They were more or less predictable in the original, and turned into an absurdity in the reworked overpriced and underfixed Def Edition. Yeah, the RC model sub-games, especially Zero's missions, became much easier. On the other hand, the actual flying missions, suffered from way too much randomness, due to those changes.

The game has not become unplayable. In many ways, it is still the San Andreas we know and love.  Yet, it is now just a game from a list of many. Not a 10/10 masterpiece, that is worth replaying every now and then.

My mark for the Definitive Edition is 7/10. While the original with some visual mods is still a much better way to cherish your nostalgia... Shame, shame, a simple burger made out of a masterpiece dish. My worst fear is that Rockstar, like many other game studios, has forgotten how and why they are so popular (it is certainly not about Shark Cards).

Its fine now, but there are issues. For some reason, they thought it was a good idea to modify how things used to control, bikes and planes for example, especially planes, I don't recall having so many problems trying to control the RC planes and regular planes on the og version as I do with this one on keyboard and mouse.

On the positive side, you can play it with higher framerate than the original with not as many game breaking bugs as the original, the only problem that remains from playing with higher framerates is that you can move cars with your characters body but outside from that, it works fine.

The game has aged well and the remaster helped it a bit

The controls are very weird though, I'm feeling like the aircrafts are way too sensitive compared to the original game which is a big issue when you have to fly them to complete the game and there's no other way around that

Overall, i would not recommend buying that if you have the original game though, you should just play the original because it's not too bad after all. I'm gonna leave a positive review just because the game is very much playable and enjoyable it the state it's in

citations.review_text: A Peak game, bugs may still be there, i dont care, thats what make a lot of old games even funner, the jank. 10/10 story 10/10 characters 8/10 grafix 1/10 plane controls

★★★★☆ Very good!

[h1]Action[/h1]

While it may not be the flawless upgrade fans originally hoped for, Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas – The Definitive Edition still delivers the ultimate sandbox experience. 

As for San Andreas itself, this game’s mission variety, customization options, and scope are impressive. Many of the missions in San Andreas also further ramp up the complexity, spectacle, and set pieces — making some of them a lot longer as a result. Thankfully, a new checkpoint system was implemented in the Definitive Edition, making it so missions can be restarted at specific moments (as opposed to entirely from the beginning).

However, no amount of checkpoints can help my frustration with the RC toy missions across this trilogy. Notably, they did add additional time to some of these to make them more manageable, but these tiny vehicle horrors control just as poorly as I remember.[hr][i][h3]Good old Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas with graphic mods.[/h3][/i][/hr]

San andreas were punching and knocking everything above its weight for its time, even to this day, modern slops still failed to match to the level of love presented in this piece of gem. Feels good to play even with the defective remake filter. The driving feels incredible, Only small issues were the plane physics which takes some time to master and tame, it took me a total of 7 hours to complete the plane achievement other than that.  Everything presented in this game reminds me of the great times of my childhood where everything were simple and happy. I would like to give this game a whopping 10/10 for me.

San Andreas is one of my favorite GTA game from the series. I love the mission slop and the weird content it has. I do prefer a more realistic roleplay game like Red Dead 2, but this game is old school so I love it for that. 

Sadly the original is gone from Steam. I do like this version better for few things. 

Whats better: 
The Hud, and weapon, and music slot is really easy to navigate. 

The restart and checkpoints for the game. IF you made a mistake then you can go back to it (but for other missions you would have to restart the whole thing which is soo annoying for new players) 

Fixing the glitches. There are some glitches in the game that can just annoy you. Like mission glitches were you have to restart because of some bug. 

Achievements. Getting 100% wasn't that hard and fun. Some of the things to do was annoying but that makes it fun.

Things I dislike: 
Fixing the glitches. There are some glitches back in the days that was funny but some of them were fix. Like trying to achievement hunt fast but can't because they fix the sex appeal glitch. 

Sadly some of the glitches aren't fix which is good but other time it can be annoying. 

The texture is so ugly. When I wanted a new version of the game I was looking for updating the texture of the game, or better shadings of everything. No, all they did was smooth everything, so they just removed the pixels and the cars and other stuff. So it looks like everything is melting. The expression faces stayed the game kinda, and nothing much. 

If you want to play retro then I recommend just playing the emulated old school Playstation 2 or Xbox or the old PC version, and I recommend making save points. 

But if you just want to try out the game the definitive edition isn't the worse. I still had fun from both games because of the game mission lore and content.
